005package org.wpilib.hardware.counter;
006
007import org.wpilib.hardware.hal.CounterJNI;
008import org.wpilib.internal.UnitTelemetry;
009import org.wpilib.telemetry.TelemetryLoggable;
010import org.wpilib.telemetry.TelemetryTable;
011import org.wpilib.units.Units;
012import org.wpilib.util.UsageReporting;
013
014/**
015 * Tachometer.
016 *
017 * <p>The Tachometer class measures the rate of digital pulses to determine the rotation velocity of
018 * a mechanism. Examples of devices that could be used with the tachometer class are a hall effect
019 * sensor, break beam sensor, or optical sensor detecting tape on a shooter wheel. Unlike encoders,
020 * this class only needs a single digital input.
021 */
022public class Tachometer implements TelemetryLoggable, AutoCloseable {
023  private final int m_handle;
024  private int m_edgesPerRevolution = 1;
025
026  /**
027   * Constructs a new tachometer.
028   *
029   * @param channel The channel of the Tachometer.
030   * @param configuration The edge configuration
031   */
032  public Tachometer(int channel, EdgeConfiguration configuration) {
033    m_handle = CounterJNI.initializeCounter(channel, configuration.rising);
034
035    UsageReporting.reportUsage("IO", channel, "Tachometer");
036  }
037
038  @Override
039  public void close() {
040    CounterJNI.freeCounter(m_handle);
041  }
042
043  /**
044   * Gets the tachometer frequency.
045   *
046   * @return Current frequency (in hertz).
047   */
048  public double getFrequency() {
049    return CounterJNI.getCounterRate(m_handle);
050  }
051
052  /**
053   * Sets the time window used to calculate the tachometer rate.
054   *
055   * @param windowMilliseconds The rate calculation window in milliseconds. Valid values are 5
056   *     through 255. The default is 50.
057   */
058  public void setRateWindow(int windowMilliseconds) {
059    CounterJNI.setCounterRateWindow(m_handle, windowMilliseconds);
060  }
061
062  /**
063   * Gets the number of edges per revolution.
064   *
065   * @return Edges per revolution.
066   */
067  public int getEdgesPerRevolution() {
068    return m_edgesPerRevolution;
069  }
070
071  /**
072   * Sets the number of edges per revolution.
073   *
074   * @param edgesPerRevolution Edges per revolution.
075   */
076  public void setEdgesPerRevolution(int edgesPerRevolution) {
077    m_edgesPerRevolution = edgesPerRevolution;
078  }
079
080  /**
081   * Gets the current tachometer revolutions per second.
082   *
083   * <p>setEdgesPerRevolution must be set with a non 0 value for this to return valid values.
084   *
085   * @return Current RPS.
086   */
087  public double getRevolutionsPerSecond() {
088    int edgesPerRevolution = getEdgesPerRevolution();
089    if (edgesPerRevolution == 0) {
090      return 0;
091    }
092    return getFrequency() / edgesPerRevolution;
093  }
094
095  /**
096   * Gets the current tachometer revolutions per minute.
097   *
098   * <p>setEdgesPerRevolution must be set with a non 0 value for this to return valid values.
099   *
100   * @return Current RPM.
101   */
102  public double getRevolutionsPerMinute() {
103    return getRevolutionsPerSecond() * 60;
104  }
105
106  /**
107   * Gets if the tachometer is stopped.
108   *
109   * <p>The tachometer is stopped when its current frequency is zero.
110   *
111   * @return True if the tachometer is stopped.
112   */
113  public boolean getStopped() {
114    return CounterJNI.getCounterStopped(m_handle);
115  }
116
117  @Override
118  public void logTo(TelemetryTable table) {
119    UnitTelemetry.log(table, "RPM", getRevolutionsPerMinute(), Units.RotationsPerMinute);
120  }
121
122  @Override
123  public String getTelemetryType() {
124    return "Tachometer";
125  }
126}
